competency_fulfillment.rationale: Nine of the seventeen samples genuinely solve a problem from graph-implied data (e.g. seed 44's 'A bar graph shows 2233 costume sash and 6570 wristband sold at the school stage. How many items were sold in total?'), but four samples (42, 43, 46, 604) are pure value-reads and four more (51, 601, 603, 605) are 'create a bar graph' tasks, neither of which solves a problem.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency calls for bar graphs '(horizontal and vertical)'; only seed 601's create-graph item ('Create a bar graph (horizontal bars) to show: Monday: 55, Tuesday: 50, Wednesday: 45, Thursday: 60') names an orientation, and it is a presenting task rather than a solving task, so the solve-a-problem items never distinguish horizontal from vertical.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The solving items use additions up to four digits (seed 44's 8803 total), which is within Grade 3 Quarter 3 computational range.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All nine genuine solve-a-problem items share the same two-item, find-the-total structure seen in seed 44's costume-sash-and-wristband item; there is no difference/comparison word problem using graph data within this node.

competency_alignment.rationale: Eight of seventeen samples (the pure reads and the create-graph items) vary along a different skill axis than 'solve problems using data', diluting the competency's intended focus.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The largest computed total, seed 602's 9099, is a reasonable scale for Grade 3 addition word problems.
